players.product: High-density AI data-center colocation / powered infrastructure (ex-Bitcoin-mining conversion)

quarterly_data.signal: Core Scientific's capital expenditures were $954.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 versus $205.3 million a year earlier, driven by conversion and expansion of data center infrastructure for colocation. As of June 30, 2026 it was contractually committed to approximately $1.0 billion of future cash expenditures under purchase and construction commitments (remaining build-out at existing customer conversion sites, the Hunt County, Texas campus and new development for prospective customers), of which $264 million will be passed through to its customer as invoiced, with substantially all expected within the next 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: capex $954.2 million (six months ended June 30, 2026) vs $205.3 million; ~$1.0 billion purchase and construction commitments, $264 million passed through to customer

connects_to.relationship: Dedicated AI data-center capacity leased to CoreWeave (12-year leases across 5+ sites)

contracts.signal: Core Scientific's 10-Q states its colocation revenue is currently derived entirely from a single customer, CoreWeave, which represented approximately 77% of total revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026; colocation revenue was 77% of total revenue versus 12% for the six months ended June 30, 2025.

Of Core Scientific's $954.2 million of capital expenditures in the six months ended June 30, 2026, $180.9 million was funded by CoreWeave pursuant to its existing colocation service agreement. The 10-Q says the CoreWeave agreement is funded almost entirely by the customer, with Core Scientific's financial contribution capped at a fixed dollar amount.
contracts.value: $180.9 million of capex funded by CoreWeave (six months ended June 30, 2026)
